SECRET SANTA DRAW · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER · NOTHING UPLOADED

Secret Santa generator: no emails, couples kept apart, organizer plays too

Type the names, say who must not draw each other and who drew whom last year, then share one link in your group chat. Each person opens it, picks their own name and sees only their person. The organizer never sees the pairings, so the organizer can play. No sign-up, no email addresses, no ads.

Running a draw with couples or family groups? Read how the rules work, with a worked example.

Find your person

You are buying for

1. Who is playing

2. Rules

A pasted link brings back its names and rules and avoids every pairing from that draw, without anyone reading them.

Add at least three names, then choose how to hand out the results.

Your group link

How it works

The draw. The page first checks, with an exact matching algorithm, that the rules leave a valid draw at all, and if not it names the people who are stuck. Then it shuffles until a draw satisfies every rule, and falls back to a depth-first search for tight rule sets. One loop covering everyone is a uniformly random circle.

The link. The group link holds the names, the rules and one random number. Opening it recomputes the same draw in the visitor's browser. Nothing is stored on a server, so there is nothing to leak, and also nothing to recover: save the link.

Honor system. Because the link contains everything needed to recompute the draw, someone determined and technical could work out every pairing. It is the hat on a table. For an airtight version on one device use Pass the phone.

Checked: the test suite draws thousands of random groups and confirms that nobody draws themselves, couples are kept apart, last year's pairs are not repeated, the no-swap and single-loop rules hold, and a link always reproduces the same draw.

Common questions

Can the organizer join without seeing who got whom?

Yes. Make a group link and share it in your group chat: the organizer never sees the pairings, and each person opens the link, picks their own name and sees only their person. The draw is worked out in each browser from a random number inside the link, so there is no server that could leak it.

How do I stop couples from drawing each other?

Type each couple or family on its own line under Can't draw each other, for example Ann, Ben. Everyone on a line is kept apart from everyone else on that line. If the rules leave someone with no one to give to, the page names the people who are stuck and says what to loosen.

How do I avoid repeating last year's pairs?

Paste last year's group link into the next-year box and the new draw avoids every pairing from that draw without anyone reading them. Or type last year's pairs as Giver > Receiver, one per line.

What is the no swaps rule?

It means if Ann gives to Ben then Ben cannot also give to Ann, so nobody buys for the person who buys for them. The single loop rule goes further and makes one big circle: Ann gives to Ben, Ben to Cara, and so on until the last person gives to Ann.

Is this really private?

The names and the draw never leave your browser and there are no accounts. A group link works on the honor system, like a hat on a table: anyone who is determined and knows how to read the link could work out every pairing. For an airtight version use Pass the phone, which reveals one person at a time on one device.

Does it cost anything?

No. It is free and open source with no ads, no sign-up and no email addresses collected.

No warranty. This tool is provided free and as-is, without warranty of any kind, express or implied. It draws names at random for a friendly gift exchange. It is not legal, financial or tax advice, and you are responsible for anything you buy, spend or agree to because of it.

Independent. Not affiliated with any gift-exchange service, retailer or brand, and none is named or ranked here.

Best-effort hosting, no SLA. These tools are free, experimental, and may be slow, broken, moved, or taken offline without notice. We do not promise uptime, backups of anything you enter, or that a URL will keep working. A group link contains your draw inside the link itself, so save it somewhere safe.

Everything runs in your browser. Names, rules and results are never uploaded; there are no accounts, cookies, or analytics vendors. Anonymous feature events (draw_made, link_made, link_opened, revealed, pass_started, list_shown, example_loaded, next_year_loaded) are counted in your own browser's local storage and are never sent anywhere.

Related tools: the event seating chart optimizer for wedding and party tables, and the volunteer shift scheduler for rotas.

Secret Santa rules for couples and no repeats, with a worked example

Every rule you add to a Secret Santa draw removes some of the possible draws. A few rules are free, and a few quietly leave almost nothing. This page counts the draws for a small group so you can see where the cliff is. The numbers below are recomputed from the generator's own engine by its test suite.

Run your own draw for free

Four people, two couples

Ann and Ben are a couple, and so are Cara and Dev. Nobody may draw themselves or their partner. That leaves Ann and Ben giving to Cara or Dev, and Cara and Dev giving to Ann or Ben.

RuleValid draws
Swaps allowed4
No swaps2
One big loop2

With swaps allowed, Ann may give to Cara while Cara gives to Ann. Forbidding that leaves only the two draws where the gifts go around in a circle: Ann to Cara to Ben to Dev to Ann, and Ann to Dev to Ben to Cara to Ann. Here "no swaps" and "one big loop" happen to mean the same thing.

When no draw exists

Three people with one couple, Ann, Ben and Cara with Ann and Ben together, have no valid draw at all: Ann and Ben can each only give to Cara, and Cara can only receive one gift. The generator tells you exactly that, naming Ann and Ben, instead of failing with a vague error.

Last year's pairs

Excluding last year's draw adds one more forbidden pair per person. Where swaps are allowed, a group of five goes from 44 valid draws to 13, and a group of eight from 14,833 to 4,738. It never makes a draw impossible on its own, but in a small group it leaves little surprise. Paste last year's group link into the next-year box and the generator applies it for you, and tells you if the combination has become impossible.

Open the free Secret Santa generator

Common questions

Why can't three people include a couple?

With three people and one couple, both halves of the couple can only give to the one remaining person, and a gift can only go to one giver. No draw exists, and the generator names the two people who are stuck so you can add a player or drop the rule.

How many people do I need if everyone is part of a couple?

Four is the minimum, and with exactly two couples there are only two valid draws, so the surprise is small. Six or more people, or a mix of couples and singles, gives a much larger set of draws.

Is a name drawn from a hat fairer than a computer draw?

Both are fair if the shuffle is. The computer draw has the advantage that it can respect rules for couples and last year's pairs, and that the organizer never has to see the result.
